'Flavio Bolsonaro heads for US after election defeat'
sources.text:
Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has left the country for the United States after losing Sunday's presidential election, three sources said on Tuesday, with the US State Department due to grant him and his family entry visas.
Bolsonaro, who has yet to concede to leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, left Brazil after refusing to comply with a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports.
The ruling relates to a money laundering probe in which he denies wrongdoing.
The location of Flavio, his wife and two daughters was not immediately clear. One source close to the family said Flavio had landed in Florida, but declined to say where.
"The State Department will issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and his family and allow them entry into the United States," a senior State Department official said.
Bolsonaro's departure threatens to deepen a rift between the two most populous nations in the Americas. Lula has accused Washington of colluding with the Bolsonaros to put them back in power.
Trump has previously alleged Flavio's father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, was a victim of judicial persecution in Brazil. The elder Bolsonaro also went to the United States after refusing to concede to Lula in 2022, when former US President Joe Biden was in office.
He eventually returned but was later given a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after his supporters stormed government buildings in Brasilia.
Trump made no mention of Flavio Bolsonaro's departure in comments to the press on Monday, but said the Brazilian vote "looked like another rigged election."
Lula, speaking in Brasilia, said he had just heard that Flavio had left the country, and called it shameful, saying he should have stayed in Brazil and proved his innocence.
Bolsonaro was favoured to win Sunday's presidential election but ended up losing in a shock result to Lula.
On Monday, he was given 24 hours to surrender his passports, but they were cancelled after the deadline lapsed, two sources said.
In a court ruling seen by Reuters, the Supreme Court cited the risk of Bolsonaro fleeing Brazil and his "significant financial resources" in ordering his passports seized.
Bolsonaro, who loses his immunity from prosecution when his Senate term ends in February, said on Monday he had no plans to flee.
"I have never thought about leaving the country," he said. "I will hand over my passports and defend myself against this travesty, which is a clear attempt to intimidate me."
His departure appeared to have caught his campaign manager off guard.
"We are surprised by the news because, just yesterday, we discussed the need for Flavio – given the 60 million votes he received – to take on this role as leader of the opposition," Senator Rogerio Marinho told reporters.
Although Bolsonaro has yet to officially concede defeat – saying on Sunday he would seek the annulment of the result over alleged voter irregularities – his Liberal Party said on Monday it acknowledged Lula's victory.
It remains unclear how Bolsonaro was able to leave the country while he was facing a 24-hour deadline to hand over his passports. A senior Federal Police official said Bolsonaro had not exited the country via any regular migration point.
Eduardo Bolsonaro, Bolsonaro's younger brother who lives in the United States, said ahead of the vote that an election loss would require a move.
"If my brother does not win, I'm in favour that he would leave the country," he told podcaster Steven Crowder this month. (Reuters)

Bolsonaro’s departure came after he failed to comply with a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports within 24 hours. The court had ordered the passports seized over a money laundering probe, in which Bolsonaro denies wrongdoing, citing concerns that he could flee Brazil and his “significant financial resources”. Two sources told Reuters that his passports were cancelled after the deadline expired.
The location of Bolsonaro, his wife and two daughters was not immediately clear. A source close to the family told Reuters that he had landed in Florida but declined to specify where.
“The State Department will issue visas to Flavio Bolsonaro and his family and allow them entry into the United States,” a senior US State Department official told Reuters.
Bolsonaro’s departure could deepen tensions between Washington and Brasil. Lula has accused the US of colluding with the Bolsonaro family to bring them back to power.
US president Donald Trump has repeatedly claimed that former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, Flavio’s father, was the target of judicial persecution. Trump also said on Monday that Brazil’s election “looked like another rigged election”, without providing evidence in the remarks cited by Reuters.
Lula, speaking in Brasilia, said he had just learned of Flavio’s departure and called it shameful, arguing that the senator should have stayed in Brazil to prove his innocence.
Flavio Bolsonaro has yet to formally concede defeat. On Sunday, he said he would seek to annul the election result over alleged voter irregularities, although his Liberal Party said on Monday that it acknowledged Lula’s victory.
The circumstances of his departure remain unclear. A senior Brazilian federal police official told Reuters that Bolsonaro had not left the country through any regular migration point.

His campaign manager, senator Rogerio Marinho, said he was surprised by reports of the departure, adding that they had discussed Bolsonaro taking on the role of opposition leader after receiving about 60 million votes.
Bolsonaro is due to lose his immunity from prosecution when his Senate term ends in February. His departure also echoes that of his father, who went to the United States after refusing to concede defeat to Lula in 2022. sources.news_title: Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro flees to US after election loss
sources.text:
The son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro lost elections to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday and refused to concede defeat.
The right-wing senator on Monday said a Supreme Court justice had ordered him to hand over his passports. Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged corruption and money laundering, and with his election loss is also set to lose his parliamentary immunity.
The 45-year-old was heading to Florida, CNN reported Tuesday, citing an anonymous official source. Other US media confirmed he was heading to the country.
The US state department said Tuesday that it would issue visas to Bolsonaro and his family, without confirming his travel plans.
A police source told AFP that the senator’s Brazilian and diplomatic passports had been cancelled, adding that “there is no formal record of Flavio Bolsonaro leaving the country.”
But he has held Italian nationality since 2023, according to an Italian parliamentary document seen by AFP.
Bolsonaro’s campaign manager Rogerio Marinho expressed shock over reports that the defeated candidate had fled Brazil.
“We still don’t have any news about his whereabouts,” he told reporters in Brasilia on Tuesday.
“I received a text message from him this morning, where he said he would let some time pass today and then would talk with us, and that was it,” Marinho said.
“That was the only communication we had.”
Scare tactic
Flavio Bolsonaro said Monday that the ban on his exit from Brazil amounted to a scare tactic.
“I never had any intention of leaving the country. I will surrender my passports and defend myself against this travesty,” he said in the video posted on Instagram.
US president Donald Trump, a close ally of Jair Bolsonaro, on Monday said Brazil’s elections were “rigged” following the defeat of Bolsonaro junior.
Flavio’s brother Eduardo, a US-based former lawmaker, maintains close ties with the White House.
Last week, he told a US podcast that Flavio Bolsonaro should leave Brazil in the event of electoral defeat, given the active probes into his activities.
In his Monday statement, Lula’s challenger also said he would lead the opposition to the leftist government.
Following Lula’s victory with 51.8% of the vote, Bolsonaro said he would seek to annul the result, citing the decision to extend polling hours over transportation difficulties that prevented some citizens from voting.
Lula had requested the extension, as had Bolsonaro over bad weather in parts of the country.
In his father’s footsteps
All bets were on a Bolsonaro win after he came out on top in the first round of elections earlier this month.
He campaigned on a pledge to liberate his father, who is under house arrest for coup-plotting after his own electoral loss to Lula in 2022.
Jair Bolsonaro never conceded defeat and left the country on the eve of his rival’s inauguration, only returning to Brazil three months later.
Separately on Tuesday, the Supreme Court ordered police to investigate alleged foreign funding of Flavio Bolsonaro’s campaign and other interference from abroad such as social media “manipulation.”
Lula’s campaign complained about interference in the election by Meta, the parent company of WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, claiming “algorithmic manipulation.”
Meta denies taking any actions to favor one side in the election, but previously said that some of Lula’s campaign ads had been mistakenly deactivated due to technical errors.

sources.text:
BRAZIL · POLITICS
Published Tuesday, 27 October, 6:02 p.m. ET · Source: US State Department, Brazilian Federal Police, Brazil’s Supreme Federal Court, Argentina’s National Migration Directorate, Planalto Palace
Key Facts
- The report Flávio Bolsonaro is reported to have left Brazil for the United States on Tuesday, 27 October 2026.
- Washington A senior State Department official says visas will be issued to him and his family.
- Brazil Federal Police cancelled his regular and diplomatic passports after he missed a Supreme Court deadline.
- Unconfirmed Asylum, a role for Secretary of State Rubio and his exact location are not confirmed by any official.
What Happened
Flávio Bolsonaro, the senator who lost Brazil’s 25 October runoff to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is reported to have left Brazil for the United States on Tuesday, 27 October. Earlier in the day his whereabouts were unknown, and Senator Rogério Marinho, a Bolsonaro ally, said, “We have no information.”
Federal Police sources say he arrived in the United States on Tuesday afternoon, and contacts at the White House told Brazilian reporters the same. No official source has confirmed his arrival.
Justice Alexandre de Moraes of the Supreme Federal Court had ordered him on Monday to hand over his regular and diplomatic passports within 24 hours, as we reported. When the deadline passed on Tuesday morning without delivery, the Federal Police cancelled both documents.
The order belongs to a sealed Supreme Court inquiry into suspected money laundering and currency evasion, and no charge against Flávio Bolsonaro is known. His allies call the case political persecution.
What Washington Has Said
A senior State Department official, speaking anonymously, said the department will issue visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family and permit their entry into the United States. The official did not say whether he has already entered or whether he has asked for asylum.
Reports that Secretary of State Marco Rubio arranged the departure come from Federal Police sources and a Trump ally, and Washington has not confirmed them. Reports that the Trump administration is preparing asylum for him are also unconfirmed.
Argentina Denies He Passed Through
Argentina’s National Migration Directorate said it has no record of Flávio Bolsonaro entering the country and that no flight plan including members of his family was filed. The presidential spokesperson also said he had not entered and that no asylum request exists.
The denials followed reports about a private jet held at Puerto Iguazú, near the Brazilian border, where aviation authorities did not authorise takeoff. Brazil’s Federal Police also contacted Argentine authorities to check a possible flight.
Why It Matters
Planalto Palace’s international advisers acknowledge that his departure could strain relations with the Trump administration, but they say it is no reason to cut ties. Restoring a pragmatic relationship is a priority for Lula’s new term, with trade, unresolved tariffs and public security on the agenda.
For US readers the test is whether a visa promise turns into protection for a foreign politician who did not comply with a court order, and what that does to trade talks with Brazil. It is not known whether Brazil will seek his return.
What Is Not Known
It is not known where Flávio Bolsonaro is, how he left Brazil or whether he has entered the United States. Nor is it known whether he has applied for asylum.
It is not known whether the United States arranged or only tolerated his departure. The charges, if any, that follow from the sealed Supreme Court inquiry are also unknown.
Frequently Asked Questions
Has Flávio Bolsonaro been granted asylum in the United States?
No official source says so. A State Department official said visas will be issued, but no asylum application or decision has been confirmed.
Did Flávio Bolsonaro pass through Argentina?
Argentina says no. Its migration directorate has no record of his entry, and the government says no asylum request exists.
Why did Brazil cancel his passports?
Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered him to surrender them within 24 hours in a sealed inquiry into suspected money laundering and currency evasion. When he did not comply, the Federal Police cancelled his regular and diplomatic passports.

By yourNEWS Media Newsroom
Brazilian Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, has left Brazil for the United States following his defeat in Sunday’s presidential runoff election against socialist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, according to multiple reports published Tuesday.
Three sources confirmed Bolsonaro’s departure to Reuters on Oct. 27. One source close to the Bolsonaro family said the former presidential candidate had already arrived in the United States, although the source declined to disclose his location.
The source also claimed that President Donald Trump’s administration had granted asylum to Bolsonaro and his immediate family. U.S. authorities had not publicly confirmed any asylum arrangement.
The development follows a Brazilian Supreme Court order requiring Bolsonaro to surrender his regular and diplomatic passports within 24 hours as part of an ongoing money laundering investigation.
Supreme Federal Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes issued the order Monday, one day after Bolsonaro lost the Oct. 25 presidential runoff to Lula.
Bolsonaro failed to meet Tuesday’s deadline, and Brazilian federal authorities subsequently canceled his passports.
It remains unclear how he departed Brazil despite the travel restriction.
A senior Brazilian Federal Police official told Reuters that Bolsonaro had not passed through an official immigration checkpoint, raising questions about the circumstances of his departure.
Earlier Tuesday, Argentine media reported that Bolsonaro had crossed into Argentina near Puerto Iguazú, with plans to board a private aircraft bound for the United States.
However, Argentine authorities said they had no immigration record confirming his entry into the country.
Reports from Brazil and Argentina subsequently indicated that the senator had continued toward the United States, although the precise route remained unverified.
CNN reported that two sources confirmed Bolsonaro’s departure, including a U.S. official who said the senator was flying to Florida.
The reports marked a significant change from Monday, when Bolsonaro publicly insisted he would remain in Brazil and contest the legal proceedings.
“I have never thought about leaving the country,” Bolsonaro said. “I will hand over my passports and defend myself against this travesty, which is a clear attempt to intimidate me.”

His Liberal Party subsequently acknowledged Lula’s victory.
The former presidential candidate faces multiple investigations involving allegations of money laundering, corruption and financial misconduct.
One investigation concerns alleged financial connections to a businessman associated with the Brazilian betting industry. Another involves accusations related to financial transfers from a banker under investigation.
Bolsonaro denies the allegations.
His departure could complicate those proceedings, particularly as he approaches the end of his Senate term in January 2027.
The legal developments have also intensified political tensions between Brazil’s left-wing government and supporters of the Bolsonaro family.
The senator’s father, Jair Bolsonaro, was sentenced to more than 27 years in prison following his conviction for involvement in an attempted coup after losing the 2022 presidential election. He remains under house arrest.
Jair Bolsonaro also traveled to Florida after his 2022 election defeat before returning to Brazil several months later.

sources.news_title: Brazil's Flávio Bolsonaro and family will get US visas after election loss, State Department says
US to issue Flávio Bolsonaro and family visas after he defied a travel ban and left Brazil
sources.text:
President Donald Trump approved allowing Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro entry into the United States following his election loss, a Trump adviser told CNN.
Trump administration officials were aware on Monday that Bolsonaro had roughly 24 hours to surrender his passport and made clear to the defeated Brazilian presidential candidate that he would be allowed entry in the US, the adviser said.
The US is issuing visas to Bolsonaro and his family, two US officials earlier told CNN.
A Brazilian source close to Bolsonaro said that the politician had feared arrest in Brazil. He is currently under investigation by the country’s highest court for alleged acts of corruption, money laundering and currency evasion. A person familiar with the situation told CNN on Tuesday afternoon that Bolsonaro had arrived in the US. It remains unclear where he landed.
It is currently unclear whether Trump and Bolsonaro spoke directly by phone prior the Brazilian politician’s departure.
Sources earlier confirmed to CNN that Bolsonaro had left Brazil for the US after losing Sunday’s presidential election. Brazil’s Federal Police canceled Bolsonaro’s passports after he failed to surrender them, affiliate CNN Brasil reported.
Speculation about his movements mounted after Argentine news outlet Infobae reported that Bolsonaro, a Trump-aligned candidate, had left Brazil via Argentina after losing Sunday’s runoff presidential election against leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The Argentine government said in a statement that it has “no record of Flávio Bolsonaro entering” the country.
Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered Bolsonaro to turn in his passports within 24 hours on Monday. CNN has reached out to Bolsonaro, his political party and the Brazilian Federal Police for comment on the senator’s whereabouts.
Bolsonaro said Brazilian police had informed him of the order in person and told him he was banned from leaving Brazil. In a video posted to Instagram on Monday, the senator denied that he intended to flee.
One of the allegations against Bolsonaro is connected to potential illegal online betting platforms, and another to the production of a biopic about his father, “Dark Horse,” which federal police believe involved funds from Banco Master, a now-collapsed bank at the heart of a $7 billion Ponzi-like scheme in 2025. Bolsonaro denies all wrongdoing.
At the time of his departure from Brazil, there were no warrants for his arrest, but according to legal analysts, the act of defying the court’s orders to surrender his passports could be enough reason for a warrant to be issued.
Right-wingers in exile
In leaving Brazil for the US, Bolsonaro joins a large community of Brazilian conservatives in exile — including his own brother Eduardo, former Brazilian intelligence chief Alexandre Ramagem and podcaster Paulo Figueiredo.
Eduardo suggested shortly before the runoff election that Flávio ought to leave Brazil if his bid for the presidency failed. On Tuesday, Eduardo called rumors that his brother had fled a “lie.”
Flávio’s journey mirrors his father’s actions after losing the 2022 presidential election. Shortly after his loss, Jair Bolsonaro decamped for Orlando, Florida, where he remained for three months. During that time, hundreds of his supporters stormed the seats of power in the capital Brasília, vandalizing the supreme court, congress and the presidential palace in an attack reminiscent of the insurrection on the US Capitol in 2021.
Bolsonaro and his allies’ efforts to overturn the 2022 election results led to the former president being sentenced to 27 years in prison. Trump, a prominent supporter of the Bolsonaro family, briefly imposed tariffs on Brazil in response to the criminal case against Jair. Trump claimed without evidence earlier this week that Lula’s victory was “rigged.”
Bolsonaro’s leaving Brazil comes directly after his surprise loss to Lula over the weekend. The conservative politician was a strong favorite to win, but Lula managed to outmaneuver Bolsonaro Sunday, earning 4.4 million more votes in the second round.
Lula told a crowd of supporters Tuesday that Bolsonaro’s flight from Brazil was “shameful” and that his opponent could have stayed in the country to fight his accusers in court.
“Regrettably, that is the Bolsonaro family for you. Brazil is their second homeland; their first homeland is the United States,” he said.
Bolsonaro initially refused to concede to Lula, saying his team would ask for the results to be annulled.
Bolsonaro’s Liberal Party reversed course days later. “We recognize the presidential election results,” party head Valdemar Costa Neto said, according to CNN Brasil. “But we believe the issues raised need to be properly clarified.”
The departure of the defeated presidential candidate appeared to catch his party off guard, his campaign manager suggested.
“We’re surprised because yesterday we talked about the need for Flávio — given the roughly 60 million votes he received — to take on this leadership role for the opposition,” Rogerio Marinho told reporters.
CNN’s Mauricio Torres and Anabella Gonzalez contributed reporting.

sources.news_title: U.S. to give visa to Brazilian election loser Bolsonaro
sources.text:
U.S. to give visa to Brazilian election loser Bolsonaro
BRASILIA, Brazil — The Trump administration plans to issue visas to defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, a senior State Department announced, confirming multiple reports that the senator fled his country following his loss.
Bolsonaro is en route to the U.S. and is likely to land in either Dallas or Miami, Folha de S.Paulo reported earlier in the day. The visas will allow Bolsonaro and his family to enter the U.S., according to the State Department official.
Bolsonaro, who is facing multiple criminal investigations in Brazil, was ordered to surrender his passports to Federal Police on Tuesday but failed to do so, according to a police official familiar with the situation. Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, whom the Bolsonaro family has long accused of political persecution, demanded he turn over the documents amid concerns the senator posed a flight risk.
Bolsonaro’s loss to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Sunday’s runoff election dealt a massive setback to a family that had sought to cement a political dynasty in Brazil. The senator had made freeing former President Jair Bolsonaro, his father who is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after his 2022 election loss, a central theme of his campaign.
Speaking in Texas on Tuesday afternoon, Donald Trump avoided mentioning Bolsonaro but reiterated his unfounded assertions that there was fraud in Brazil’s election. He assailed Democrats as the “greatest cheaters of elections” before adding that “Brazil’s doing a pretty good job also.”
Bolsonaro’s whereabouts were unknown to police or allies on Tuesday morning after Infobae reported that he had crossed into Argentina and planned to travel to the U.S. from there. Brazil police have no official record of Bolsonaro leaving Brazil, and the press secretary for Argentina President Javier Milei denied that he’d entered the country.
Multiple Bolsonaro allies told Bloomberg News that they tried to contact him but had not heard back.
The saga has set social media alight with memes referring to Bolsonaro as “Flyvio,” comparing him to Carmen Sandiego or Where’s Waldo? Others have altered the conservative slogan, “God, Country and Family” to “Goodbye, Country and Family.”
Bolsonaro is facing at least two federal investigations into allegations of money laundering, one of which stems from his links to the former Banco Master SA owner caught in Brazil’s biggest-ever bank fraud case. He’s denied wrongdoing.
His actions since the Sunday vote had evoked those of his father even before the reports he was leaving Brazil. He initially said he would request the annulment of the results due to a Supreme Court decision to extend voting hours, echoing Jair Bolsonaro’s refusal to accept his narrow loss to Lula four years ago.
Jair Bolsonaro left Brazil for the U.S. after the defeat. He returned months later and was subsequently barred from holding public office for eight years for spreading false claims about Brazil’s electronic voting system ahead of the election, then convicted of plotting a coup.
Supreme Court drama
Flávio Bolsonaro backed down on his plans to seek annulment of the results Monday, publishing a social media video in which he said the Supreme Court had barred him from leaving Brazil. He said the move followed comments by his brother Eduardo, who said on a podcast that Flávio should leave Brazil if he lost the election.
Moraes’ decision irritated officials in Lula’s government as well as some members of the Supreme Court, according to people familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified discussing private conversations.
Lula’s administration had wanted to focus on efforts to pacify the country and move past the polarization that has exploded during back-to-back election battles between the leftist leader and a member of the Bolsonaro family, the people said. It viewed the move from Moraes, a controversial judge who oversaw Jair Bolsonaro’s trial and has long drawn charges of censorship from the Brazilian right, as counter to those aims.
Earlier Tuesday, Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino ordered federal authorities to open an investigation into possible illegal foreign financing of Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign, including by a group linked to U.S. Vice President JD Vance.
The justice stressed that the order doesn’t establish that illegal foreign financing occurred, but said allegations leveled during Brazil’s presidential race warrant an investigation. Vance’s office didn’t respond to a request for comment.
Argentina’s spokesman, Adrian Ravier, said there had been no request for asylum in Argentina from Bolsonaro during a press conference Tuesday.
_____
